questions.skill: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single quantity
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: An investment of P dollars is worth P(1 + r)^n dollars after n years, where r > 0. Treating (1 + r)^n as one quantity, explain why the investment grows.
questions.prompt_markup:
An investment of P dollars is worth P(1 + r)^n dollars after n years, where r > 0.
Treating (1 + r)^n as one quantity, explain why the investment grows.
questions.correct_answer: Since r > 0, 1 + r > 1, so (1 + r)^n > 1 for n > 0. P times a number greater than 1 is greater than P.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation that treats (1 + r)^n as one factor greater than 1.

questions.skill: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single quantity
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: For which value of x is 10 - (x - 3)² greatest, and what is that greatest value? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup: For which value of x is 10 - (x - 3)² greatest, and what is that greatest value? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: At x = 3 the value is 10. (x - 3)² is never negative and is 0 only at x = 3, so subtracting it gives at most 10.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the x-value, the greatest value, and the reason.

questions.prompt: Which expression is never greater than 4, for every real number x?

questions.prompt: A square picture with side s is surrounded by a frame 2 units wide on every side. The frame's area is (s + 4)² - s². What do (s + 4)² and s² represent?
questions.prompt_markup:
A square picture with side s is surrounded by a frame 2 units wide on every side. The frame's area is (s + 4)² - s².
What do (s + 4)² and s² represent?
questions.correct_answer: (s + 4)² is the area of the whole framed square (side s + 2 + 2); s² is the area of the picture. Their difference is the frame.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording. Both meanings are required.

questions.prompt: A town of 5,000 people grows 3% per year: P = 5,000(1.03)^t. When will it reach 8,000? Round to the nearest tenth of a year. (log means base 10.)
questions.prompt_markup: A town of 5,000 people grows 3% per year: P = 5,000(1.03)^t. When will it reach 8,000? Round to the nearest tenth of a year. (log means base 10.)
questions.grading_note: Form required: rounded to the nearest tenth. 1.03^t = 1.6, so t = log 1.6 ÷ log 1.03 ≈ 15.90.
